mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months, accompanied by a rise in average hourly earnings (proxied by PAYEMS growth), signals a tight labor market with upward wage pressure, which erodes corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for 3 consecutive months AND PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six months signals an extended period of monetary accommodation, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer-driven economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises AND GDPC1 falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals a sudden deterioration in labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by > 0.5pp in one month (i.e., rate rises by > 0.5pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
